requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

hunches.claim: UntrustedData's object-graph depth limit is raised from 500 to 5000, so existing deserialization callers now accept payloads that previously exceeded the security limit, weakening denial-of-service protection. This runtime behavior change is unrelated to REQ-2283.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a payload containing 501 nested arrays using MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData), asserting that deserialization throws for exceeding the depth limit. The test passes against the base build (limit 500) and fails against the head build (limit 5000).

hunches.claim: The change weakens the depth-limit denial-of-service protection for untrusted input: MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth rises from 500 to 5000, allowing ten times deeper object graphs and increasing stack/CPU exhaustion risk during deserialization. This security weakening is unrelated to the generator/analyzer crash fix.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a payload nested 501 levels deep using MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). The test should require rejection for exceeding MaximumObjectGraphDepth; it passes with the base value of 500 and fails with the changed value of 5000.

hunches.claim: The change weakens the deliberate UntrustedData recursion limit from 500 to 5000, an unrelated security regression that permits substantially deeper hostile object graphs and increases stack-exhaustion denial-of-service risk.

receipt_plan.detail: Add or run a securityDefaults test asserting MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth == 500; the changed line fails it. Ledger [L9] records the stack depth limit of 500 as deliberate secure-by-default behavior.

hunches.claim: The unrelated change to UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth has no accompanying test asserting the security limit, so regressions in this value would pass unnoticed.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs:38 off-by-one: MaximumObjectGraphDepth = 5000 -> MaximumObjectGraphDepth = 5001; expected to survive because the only added tests are source-generator tests and none asserts UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth.

hunches.claim: The new tests exercise suppression of metadata diagnostics but never assert that an in-compilation diagnostic still passes ReportIfLocatedInCompilation; a regression suppressing every diagnostic would satisfy all added tests.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1445 negate-condition: diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree) -> !(diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)); expected to survive in the added tests because every usage compilation expects zero diagnostics, while the metadata diagnostic remains filtered.

hunches.claim: The fix leaves the third unguarded metadata-symbol diagnostic path at TypeCollector.cs:735 unchanged. Indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] there can still throw for a symbol with no source declaration, and wrapping reportDiagnostic cannot help because the index is evaluated before the diagnostic is passed to ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. Thus the acceptance criterion that diagnostics needing source locations not crash on metadata symbols is only partially implemented.

receipt_plan.detail: Inspect the diagnostic construction at TypeCollector.cs:735 and the new wrapper at TypeCollector.cs:236. The former still directly indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], whereas the two later sites were changed to null-tolerant helpers. Constructing that diagnostic evaluates the indexing expression before reportDiagnostic or ReportIfLocatedInCompilation is invoked.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Dropping diagnostics for metadata-only types and documenting that their defining assemblies own member validation is deliberate product behavior, not a regression in the crash fix.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] records that referenced-assembly types are deliberately not analyzed by the consuming compilation and receive no formatter or MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostics there; the defining assembly owns validation and formatting.
